doc.citation: Breuer P., Dislaire G., Filatoff J., Pirard E. & Steemans P. (2007). A classification of spores by support vectors based on an analysis of their ornament spatial distribution – An application to Emsian miospores from Saudi Arabia. In: Steemans P. & Javaux E. (eds.), Recent Advances in Palynology. Carnets de Géologie / Notebooks on Geology, Memoir 2007/01, Abstract 02, pp. 9–15.
doc.comment: Reuses borehole material studied by Breuer et al. (2005a), Stratigraphic palynology of Devonian boreholes from northern Saudi Arabia, and Breuer et al. (in press), Early to Middle Devonian miospores from northern Saudi Arabia. Member-level summaries and illustrated samples overlap and must not be counted as independent sampling. Figure 2 names JNDL-3 for Rhabdosporites minutus, whereas the geological account discusses JNDL-4. Hammamiyat assemblages are dated mid Emsian by spores, while cited brachiopod evidence suggests late Emsian. The morphotypes analysed computationally are not given taxonomic names.

items.depth_or_level: upper part of the Sha'iba Member
items.age_basis_detail: Assigned to the PoW Oppel Zone; Dictyotriletes subgranifer may indicate its uppermost Su Interval Zone. The quoted age applies to the suggested Su assignment. Separately cited trilobites and conodonts indicate Pragian-early Emsian for the uppermost Sha'iba and Qasr members.
items.notes: Pooled member-level assemblage summary; individual occurrences are not allocated between BAQA-1 and BAQA-2. Overlaps the separately listed illustrated samples, whose member assignments are not supplied. An unnamed trilete-spore lineage first appears in this interval. Reworking is mentioned only as a general possible influence on morphological signals, not demonstrated in this material.
items.locator: Introduction – Geological setting, pp. 9–10; Biostratigraphy, pp. 10–11; Figure 2

items.depth_or_level: Qasr Member and lower part of the Subbat Member
items.age_basis_detail: Assemblages probably belong to either the AB or lower FD Oppel Zones. Emphanisporites schultzii and ? Knoxisporites riondae first appear in the Qasr Member. Separately cited trilobites and conodonts indicate Pragian-early Emsian for the uppermost Sha'iba and Qasr members.
items.notes: Similar assemblages are reported throughout this interval; the two named taxa are explicitly introduced as first appearances in the Qasr Member. Their persistence in every sample is not stated. Illustrated samples are also listed separately. Reworking is discussed only as a general methodological possibility.
items.locator: Introduction – Geological setting, p. 10; Biostratigraphy, p. 11; Figure 2

items.locality: near Baq'a, Widyan Basin; near Domat Al-Jandal, Tabuk Basin
items.depth_or_level: upper part of the Subbat Member
items.age_basis_detail: First appearance of Rhabdosporites minutus marks the base of the FD Oppel Zone, Min Interval Zone.
items.notes: The geological account places the upper Subbat interval within the boreholes listed, but does not specify which contains the cited first appearance. Figure 2.8 illustrates Rhabdosporites minutus from JNDL-3, a borehole absent from that account; its identity is retained separately without correction. Reworking is discussed only generally.
items.locator: Introduction – Geological setting, p. 10; Biostratigraphy, p. 11; Figure 2.8

items.locality: near Baq'a, Widyan Basin; near Domat Al-Jandal, Tabuk Basin
items.depth_or_level: Hammamiyat Member; BAQA-1 and BAQA-2 reach only the lowermost Hammamiyat
items.age_basis_detail: Assemblages assigned to the Min Interval Zone of the FD Oppel Zone. The geological introduction separately reports a late Emsian age suggested by brachiopods.
items.notes: Spore assemblages are described as essentially similar throughout the member, but no named species is explicitly allocated to it. The unnamed trilete-spore lineage disappears in its upper part. Named taxa from adjacent intervals have not been extrapolated into this assemblage. Reworking is discussed only generally.
items.locator: Introduction – Geological setting, p. 10; Biostratigraphy, pp. 10–11
